summary.tldr: Combines hardware-aware Neural Architecture Search (MnasNet) and NetAdapt algorithms with Squeeze-and-Excitation attention and the computationally efficient hard-swish activation function.
keyTakeaways: Hardware-aware NAS optimizes both top-1 accuracy and measured real-device CPU latency.
Introduced hard-swish h-swish(x) = x * ReLU6(x + 3) / 6 to replace expensive sigmoid exponential activations.
MobileNetV3 Large is 3.2% more accurate and 20% faster than MobileNetV2.

motivation.problemStatement: Manual micro-architectural block tuning is slow, and FLOP count is an imperfect proxy for actual on-device latency because memory access cost varies across layers.
previousLimitations: FLOP-optimized models do not always correlate with low real-world device execution times.
Standard Swish activation f(x) = x * sigmoid(x) requires expensive exponential calculation on mobile CPUs.
Last stage classification heads in MobileNetV2 incurred high latency overhead.
motivation.coreInsight: We can combine platform-aware NAS (MnasNet) to find coarse block structures, NetAdapt to fine-tune individual layer channel counts, and hard-swish non-linearities to eliminate floating point exponential bottlenecks.
contributions: Formulated MobileNetV3 Large and Small model specifications.
Designed the hard-swish (h-swish) and hard-sigmoid (h-sigmoid) non-linearities.
Redesigned the expensive network stem and classification tail for 7% latency reduction.

innovations.title: Hard-Swish (h-swish) Non-Linearity
innovations.summary: Replaces exponential sigmoid calculations in Swish with a computationally efficient piecewise linear ReLU6 approximation.
innovations.detailedDescription: Swish x * sigmoid(x) improves deep network accuracy but is expensive to compute on mobile hardware. Hard-swish replaces sigmoid with ReLU6(x + 3) / 6, eliminating exponential lookup tables.

math.explanation: Piecewise linear approximation of Swish activation using optimized ReLU6 primitives.
math.significance: Eliminates memory and instruction latency overhead of computing e^-x on mobile CPUs.

ablationStudies.title: Impact of h-swish in Deeper vs Shallower Layers
ablationStudies.description: Tested applying h-swish across all layers vs applying h-swish only in deeper layers (using ReLU in shallow layers).
ablationStudies.performanceDelta: Using h-swish only in deeper layers retained accuracy while saving computation, as memory bandwidth dominates early layer runtime.

evidence.reproducibilityNotes: Trained using RMSProp with 0.9 momentum, weight decay 1e-5, and exponential learning rate decay on TPUs.

criticalNotes.title: Optimal On-Device Latency/Accuracy Tradeoff
criticalNotes.content: Delivers state-of-the-art inference throughput on mobile CPU and NPU hardware targets.

criticalNotes.title: High Micro-Architectural Complexity
criticalNotes.content: Each layer block contains custom channel width multipliers, kernel sizes, and SE-ratios, making manual edits complex.

lineage.title: MobileNetV2: Inverted Residuals and Linear Bottlenecks
lineage.description: Predecessor architecture providing inverted residual blocks.

lineage.title: Learning Transferable Architectures for Scalable Image Recognition

researchGaps: Can MobileNetV3 blocks be adapted to Vision Transformer attention layers?

reference.originalAbstract: We present the next generation of MobileNets based on a combination of complementary search techniques as well as a novel architecture design. MobileNetV3 is tuned to mobile phone CPUs through a combination of hardware-aware neural architecture search (NAS) complemented by the NetAdapt algorithm.
